talk_track: I do technology governance for charter and independent school networks — the board-facing layer that sits above whichever IT vendor a school already uses, and never replaces them. Your live Operations Associate posting for HLA lists, among the duties of a $50,000-$60,000 role it describes as ideal for someone early in their career: "Assists with technology (e.g. liaising with our IT vendor, navigating mandatory systems, check-out and return of materials, tracking student and staff tech inventory, etc.)." The Philadelphia version of the same role owns "secure collection, transfer, and storage of sensitive student records." Read together, those lines say the person overseeing your IT vendor and holding student data is the newest person in the building — that's a governance gap, not a hiring one. It's also the difference I've watched decide whether a vendor breach costs a school days of parent communication or weeks. Could your board name your IT vendors today?
